title: GPA Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: GPA Calculator: Weighted GPA from grades and credit hours. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Weighted GPA from grades and credit hours. Enter your grades (letters or points, comma separated) and credits for each course and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Grade Point Average converts letter grades into points on a 4.0 scale and weights them by credit hours. It's the standard measure used by US colleges and many universities worldwide. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Education tools include [Final Grade Calculator](/grade-calculator), [Test Score Calculator](/test-score-calculator) and [Weighted Average Calculator](/weighted-average-calculator).

## How to use the GPA Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your grades (letters or points, comma separated), then typing or pasting your credits for each course. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Type or paste your grades (letters or points, comma separated).
2. Type or paste your credits for each course.
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

GPA = Σ(grade points × credits) ÷ Σcredits. A = 4.0, A− = 3.7, B+ = 3.3, B = 3.0 …

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A (3 cr), B+ (4 cr), A− (3 cr), B (3 cr), A (2 cr) gives 52.3 quality points over 15 credits = 3.49 GPA. Try the same figures in the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Grades (letters or points, comma separated): A, B+, A-, B, A, Credits for each course: 3, 4, 3, 3, 2), the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) returns GPA: 3.55, Total credits: 15, Quality points: 53.3. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Final Grade Calculator](/grade-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- High-credit courses affect GPA the most.
- Check your school's scale — some give A+ = 4.3.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good GPA?

3.0 is generally considered good, and 3.5+ is strong for competitive programmes. Try it with your own numbers in the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I enter numeric grades?

Yes — enter grade points like 3.7 instead of letters. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### How can I raise my GPA?

GPA is a weighted average, so the fastest way up is higher grades in your remaining and heaviest-weighted courses. Where your school allows it, retaking a failed course can also lift the average. Try it with your own numbers in the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the GPA Calculator use?

GPA = Σ(grade points × credits) ÷ Σcredits. A = 4.0, A− = 3.7, B+ = 3.3, B = 3.0 … You can see it in action in the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

Yes. The GPA Calculator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [GPA Calculator](/gpa-calculator) and start straight away.
